prompt: `WeekSummary` declares `readonly planned = input.required<number>()`. What happens if a template writes `<app-week-summary />` without `[planned]`?

choices.text: The summary shows `undefined minutes planned`
choices.why: That is what `.required` exists to prevent.

choices.text: The build fails
choices.why: Right. A required input must be bound where the component is used.

choices.text: `planned` falls back to 0
choices.why: Only `input(0)`, with a default, falls back; a required one has none.

choices.text: The summary loads the number from the file itself
choices.why: The summary no longer knows about the file.

prompt: After the week passed its numbers down as inputs, how many requests for `/courses.json` did the page make?

choices.text: Two, one per component, as in lesson 6
choices.why: The summary stopped loading the file.

choices.text: One
choices.why: Right. Only the week loads it now.

choices.text: None, because inputs are filled at build time
choices.why: Inputs are set while the page runs; the week still had to load.

choices.text: Three, one per course card
choices.why: The cards receive their course; they load nothing.

prompt: Why are the inputs `readonly` but not `protected`?

choices.text: `protected` would hide them from the component's own template
choices.why: The own template reads `protected` fields fine.

choices.text: Signals cannot be `protected`
choices.why: They can; the planner's computed signals are.

choices.text: The parent's template sets them, so they are public
choices.why: Right. They are part of the component's face to its users.

choices.text: `readonly` and `protected` cannot be combined
choices.why: The planner combines them on almost every field.

prompt: A parent passes a value to a child's input by writing the input's name, in the child's tag, inside square ___.
`<app-course-page courseId="javascript" />` has no brackets. What does `courseId` receive?

choices.text: The text `javascript`
choices.why: Right. Without brackets, the value is a plain string.

choices.text: The value of a field called `javascript`
choices.why: That is what `[courseId]="javascript"` would read, and there is no such field.

choices.text: Nothing until the router sets it in lesson 17
choices.why: The attribute sets it now; the router takes over later.

choices.text: A build error, because inputs need brackets
choices.why: Brackets are for expressions; a constant string needs none.

prompt: In the error state, why must the template check `data.error()` before reading `course()`?

choices.text: `course()` returns `undefined` in that state, which hides the error
choices.why: It does not return `undefined`: reading the value throws.

choices.text: Because `value()` throws when the resource failed
choices.why: Right. The test of the App failed exactly this way before the branch was added.

choices.text: Because `@if` branches must be in alphabetical order
choices.why: Order matters for meaning, not alphabet.

choices.text: Because `error()` resets the resource
choices.why: Reading `error()` changes nothing.

prompt: `sessions` uses `.filter(…).sort(…)` on the resource's array. Why does that not break lesson 6's rule about changing a signal's value in place?

choices.text: `sort` never changes the array it is called on
choices.why: It does; that is why the order of calls matters.

choices.text: `filter` returns a new array, and `sort` reorders that one
choices.why: Right. The array in the resource is untouched.

choices.text: Arrays inside a resource are frozen by Angular
choices.why: Angular freezes nothing; the code has to avoid it.

choices.text: A computed may change what it reads
choices.why: A computed must not change anything it reads.

choices.text: The DOM `change` event of the checkbox
choices.why: That event stayed inside the row; the list emitted its own value.

choices.text: The session object that was ticked
choices.why: The list emitted an id and a boolean, not the session.

choices.text: The value the list passed to `emit`
choices.why: Right. For a component's output, `$event` is whatever was emitted.

choices.text: A copy of the list's inputs
choices.why: Inputs do not travel back up.

prompt: Why does `SessionRow` emit `toggled` instead of setting `session().done = true` itself?

choices.text: An input cannot be read inside an event handler
choices.why: The handler reads it; the point is who changes the data.

choices.text: `done` is a private field of `Session`
choices.why: `Session` is an interface with public fields.

choices.text: The data belongs to the page, which decides
choices.why: Right. The row reports; the owner changes, with a new value.

choices.text: Emitting is faster than assigning
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: After the 24th's session was ticked on the course page, the week still said `90 done`. Why?

choices.text: The week only recomputes once a day
choices.why: It recomputes when its own data changes, and its data did not.

choices.text: OnPush stopped the week from being checked
choices.why: OnPush skips what nothing marked, and nothing changed the week's data.

choices.text: The week has its own copy of the data
choices.why: Right. Two owners of one truth; lesson 11 gives the data a single owner.

choices.text: The change was only saved to the server
choices.why: There is no server yet; the change lived in the page's resource.

prompt: Match each declaration with what it is for.

pairs.right: data the parent must hand down
a value passed down that the child may change
an element of the component's own template

right_distractors: a value worked out from other signals

prompt: `[(value)]="minutes"` on the stepper is shorthand for what?

choices.text: `[value]="minutes()"` alone, read twice
choices.why: That would only pass the value down.

choices.text: `[value]="minutes()"` plus `(valueChange)="minutes.set($event)"`
choices.why: Right. `model` declares the `valueChange` output for you.

choices.text: `(value)="minutes"`, an output only
choices.why: The value also goes down; that is the first half.

choices.text: A `@let` that copies `minutes`
choices.why: `@let` is read-only and local to the template.

prompt: The bench's `minutes` started at 45. What did it hold after two clicks on `5 more`?
Why does the lesson not use `model()` for a session's `done` in the planner?

choices.text: `model` only works with numbers
choices.why: It works with any type.

choices.text: Checkboxes cannot be bound two ways
choices.why: They can; the reason is ownership.

choices.text: `model` is deprecated in Angular 21
choices.why: It is current.

choices.text: The row would change the owner's data behind its back
choices.why: Right. `model` is for a control's value; data that belongs to somebody gets an input and an output.

prompt: The panel has `<ng-content select="h2" />` before `<ng-content />`. The week writes its `<h2>` first anyway. What would happen if the week wrote the `<h2>` last?

choices.text: The heading would appear last
choices.why: The panel's slot decides where the `<h2>` goes, not the parent's order.

choices.text: The heading would still appear first
choices.why: Right. `select="h2"` takes it wherever the parent wrote it.

choices.text: The heading would appear twice
choices.why: Each element goes to one slot only.

choices.text: The build would fail, because slots require order
choices.why: Order in the parent is free.

prompt: Whose stylesheet styles the projected `<h2>` inside the panel?

choices.text: The week's
choices.why: Right. Projected content belongs to the parent that wrote it.

choices.text: The panel's, since the heading sits inside its section
choices.why: The panel's styles reach only its own template's elements.

choices.text: Both, merged
choices.why: Each element carries one component's attribute.

choices.text: Neither: projected content is unstyled
choices.why: The parent's styles apply to it as usual.

choices.text: The input element itself, as a plain field
choices.why: It returns a signal, holding a wrapper whose `nativeElement` is the element.

choices.text: A signal holding an `ElementRef`
choices.why: Right. `.nativeElement` is the input.

choices.text: The text typed into the input
choices.why: It gives the element; the text is its `value`.

choices.text: A list of every element named `note` on the page
choices.why: It looks in its own template, and returns one.

prompt: After the required input was added, the generated `WeekSummary` test failed with `NG0950`. What fixed it?

choices.text: Making the inputs optional so the test passes
choices.why: That weakens the component to suit the test.

choices.text: Deleting the test
choices.why: Lesson 24 writes better tests; deleting this one fixes nothing.

choices.text: `fixture.componentRef.setInput` for both
choices.why: Right. A test is a parent and must provide what is required.

choices.text: Running the test with `--watch`
choices.why: Watching reruns the same failure.

prompt: A new `SessionBadge` component shows a session's minutes and, when clicked, asks to delete it. Which declarations does it need?

choices.text: A `model` for the session, so it can delete it
choices.why: Deleting is the owner's job; the badge reports.

choices.text: A `viewChild` to the parent's list
choices.why: A child never reaches up into its parent.

choices.text: An input for the session and an output for the request
choices.why: Right. Data down, news up.

choices.text: Two outputs, one for the minutes and one for the click
choices.why: The minutes come down; only the request goes up.
